title: Strict reduction and normalized realization of completed open extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$, $T=U,X$, and identify $j^{-1}\widehat R_X=\widehat R_U$. Use the strict semilinear system category, reduction/total-limit adjunction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Let $J_j$ be exact termwise system extension by zero, and let $j_!$ be localized ringed-site extension by zero for the completed coefficient sheaves [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

For any derived-complete $K\in D(\widehat R_U)$, with completeness meaning the quotient-tower condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], extension by zero on a flat-term K-flat reduction representative induces a specified natural isomorphism of derived semilinear systems
$$r_j(K):\mathcal R_X(j_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R_UK.$$
Its evaluation at $n$ is the canonical open-tensor coefficient isomorphism $(j_!K)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X\cong j_!(K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_U}(A_n)_U)$, and it respects every strict quotient transition. The object $j_!K$ is derived complete. If $u_{j_!K}$ denotes the actual reduction/total-limit unit, then it is invertible and
$$d_j(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_j(K))^{-1}:\mathcal L_XJ_j\mathcal R_UK\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!K.$$
With the corresponding completed restriction pullback, this comparison identifies the realized open adjunction unit and counit with the localized ringed-site unit and counit. These are comparisons of the specified simultaneous section constructions of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], not choices of lifts of their evaluations.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), with sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor). Agent-formulated strict varying-coefficient open comparison, its quotient-completion unit and open-adjunction normalization, extracted from step 3 of the realization proof; completeness input is lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison.

proof.text: First record normalization for any ambient $P$. Choose one flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ as in [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For $m\ge n$, $Q\otimes B_m$ is K-flat over $B_m$: its tensor with an acyclic $B_m$-complex $F$ is $Q\otimes\operatorname{Res}F$, which is acyclic because scalar restriction is exact and $Q$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The transition-adjoint is therefore the balancing isomorphism $(Q\otimes B_m)\otimes_{B_m}B_n\to Q\otimes B_n$, $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(a)b$, with inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$. For three quotients both composites multiply by the same image of $a$ and $b$. Hence $\mathcal R_TP$ is normalized, with its actual strict quotient transitions [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus].

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT; explicit quotient balancing on the reduction model

proof.text: For any $P$ satisfying [def-weil-derived-complete], the actual unit $u_P$ is invertible, not merely some map with the same projections. Indeed put $N=\mathcal R_TP$, normalized by Step 1. The coherent counit $e_N$ is invertible by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] and evaluation detection in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The triangle identity in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] gives $\mathcal L_T(e_N)\circ u_{\mathcal L_TN}=1$, so $u_{\mathcal L_TN}=\mathcal L_T(e_N)^{-1}$ is invertible. The total-limit Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and the existence-of-isomorphism clause of the completeness definition, give an isomorphism $a:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_TN$. Naturality says $u_{\mathcal L_TN}\circ a=(\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_Ta)\circ u_P$. All other factors are invertible; thus $u_P$ is invertible. The isomorphism $a$ is used only to prove invertibility; it does not define or replace $u_P$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; formal triangle identity for the specified reduction/limit adjunction

proof.text: The datum $(A,I)=(R,(t))$ satisfies the hypotheses needed for [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] and [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. In fact [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] makes $R$ a PID domain, hence Noetherian since every ideal is generated by one element; $t\ne0$. The quotients are finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], and their residue field has characteristic $\ell$, so $R/(t)$ is additive torsion. The exact sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{t^n}R\to R/t^n\to0$ is a length-one finite-free resolution, proving that every quotient is perfect. Since every $R/t^n$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] identifies the constant sheaf $(A_n)_T$ with the coefficient sheaf $(P_n)_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], hence $\widehat R_T=A_T$ and the two module categories coincide. For $K$ with flat-term K-flat representative $Q$, the strict quotient tower $K_\bullet=(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_T}(A_n)_T)_n$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is $U_T\mathcal R_TK$, and the quotient completion map $\operatorname{comp}_K$ in [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] is exactly $u_K$: both are the total limit of the one strict tower map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ from the constant tower on $Q$, not just maps with the same derived evaluations [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The unit-respecting isomorphism $c_K\circ\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$ and Step 2 show that $\kappa_K$ is invertible. Thus $K$ satisfies the intrinsic Koszul completeness hypothesis of the completed extension theorem [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion].

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; quotient comparison recorded by prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] to $j$ and the identity base-change square ($X'=X$, $U'=U$). Its quasi-compactness hypothesis is precisely the hypothesis on $j$ here; no finite-type or constructibility assumption on $K$ is used. It gives intrinsic completeness of $M=j_!K$. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], its canonical quotient completion map $\operatorname{comp}_M=u_M$ is invertible, with the equality of constructions as in Step 3. Transporting the total-limit Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] through $u_M$ gives a distinguished triangle whose first map has components the actual reductions of $M$. This is exactly [def-weil-derived-complete], proving the requested quotient-tower completeness and invertibility of the actual $u_{j_!K}$.

Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The exact extension/restriction adjunction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] represents $j_!K$ by $j_!P$. This is again flat-term K-flat. For a flat term $P^a$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] identifies tensor by $j_!P^a$ with the composite $F\mapsto j_!(P^a\otimes j^*F)$, which is exact, proving flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. For an acyclic complex $F$, the same natural tensor identity totalizes to $(j_!P)\otimes F\cong j_!(P\otimes j^*F)$. Here $j_!$ commutes with the direct sums by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]; naturality commutes with the two differentials and hence with $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Exactness of $j^*$, K-flatness of $P$, then exactness of $j_!$ make the right side acyclic. This proves K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I; K-flat verification expanded

proof.text: Use the canonical tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] with $M=K$ and $N=(A_n)_X$. On the models of Step 5 it gives $(j_!P)\otimes_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X\cong j_!(P\otimes_{\widehat R_U}(A_n)_U)$. These chain maps are natural in the coefficient sheaf: for $q:(A_{n+1})_X\to(A_n)_X$, either route takes $x\otimes a$ over the open to $x\otimes q(a)$; globally the same equality follows from the adjunct defining the canonical comparison and its naturality. Thus the squares with every strict transition commute before localization. They define an isomorphism of complexes in the strict semilinear category, hence a specified isomorphism $r_j(K):\mathcal R_Xj_!K\to J_j\mathcal R_UK$. The reduction functor uses exactly these models [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Independence and naturality in derived $K$, as well as the simultaneous section interpretation, follow from [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], applied to these tensor/open constructions. Its evaluation is the stated canonical tensor map. This constructs one system map; no family of evaluated arrows is lifted after the fact.

source.place: Tags 0GL1 and 0E8I, natural open tensor comparison; simultaneous models as specified in the cited section theorem

proof.text:
Since $r_j(K)$ identifies $J_j\mathcal R_UK$ with a reduction system, Step 1 makes it normalized. Step 4 and functoriality of $\mathcal L_X$ give the natural isomorphism $d_j(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L_X(r_j(K))^{-1}$. There is a useful normalization identity in the actual derived system category:
$$r_j(K)\circ\mathcal R_X(d_j(K))=e_{J_j\mathcal R_UK}.$$
To verify it, the triangle identity gives $\mathcal R_X(u_{j_!K}^{-1})=e_{\mathcal R_Xj_!K}$; naturality of $e$ for $r_j(K)$ gives the displayed equation after composing with $\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_X(r_j(K))^{-1}$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Thus the specified inverse unit, rather than an arbitrary reconstruction isomorphism, normalizes $d_j$.

source.place: Tag 0941 total-limit functor; formal naturality and triangle identities

proof.text: For a complete $H$ on $X$, [lem-sf-immersion-completed-pullback-comparison] applied to the open immersion $j$ identifies completed restriction with ordinary exact $j^*$ and says $j^*H$ is complete, including its finite projections and completion comparison. Write $P_j$ for termwise system restriction and $s_H:\mathcal R_Uj^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j\mathcal R_XH$ for restriction of the quotient tensor models. The restriction/tensor identifications of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], modeled simultaneously by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], give this actual system isomorphism, respecting all quotient transitions. Hence the realized right adjoint in the assertion is the specified completed restriction, with this comparison.

source.place: Tags 0GL1 and 0941; restriction comparison of the cited immersion theorem

proof.text:
Let $\eta^o,\epsilon^o$ be the localized ringed-site open unit and counit and $\eta^S,\epsilon^S$ their termwise-system counterparts. The tensor comparison defining $r$ is normalized by the open unit [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Consequently
$$P_j(r_j(K))\circ s_{j_!K}\circ\mathcal R_U(\eta^o_K)=\eta^S_{\mathcal R_UK}.$$
Indeed on a flat-term model over an object factoring through $U$, both composites send $x\otimes a$ to that same section $x\otimes a$. This is the adjunction-unit characterization of the canonical tensor comparison, so gives the equality globally by the open adjunction, not by testing arbitrary derived morphisms on evaluations. The exact localized-site adjunction is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] preserves these units and transposes simultaneously on localization. Thus the equation holds as an equality of system transformations.

source.place: Tag 0GL1; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI, 03DJ and 0E8I, open-adjunction normalization

proof.text:
Taking the open adjunction transposes of the unit compatibility in Step 9 gives the counit equation
$$\mathcal R_X(\epsilon^o_H)=\epsilon^S_{\mathcal R_XH}\circ J_j(s_H)\circ r_j(j^*H).$$
More explicitly, the transpose of either side is the identity of $P_j\mathcal R_XH$ after $s_H$, by the triangle identities; the adjunction Hom bijection is injective. These are the specified simultaneous transposes of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. To pass to realization, Step 2 gives invertible units on all complete inputs and [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] gives invertible counits on normalized systems. Thus $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$ restricts to inverse equivalences on these subcategories; in particular $\mathcal R$ is faithful there. Step 7 says precisely that reduction of $d_j$ is the canonical counit comparison. Apply the equivalences to the two displayed unit/counit equations and use their natural units and counits [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Together with $s_H$ from Step 8, they identify the realized open unit and counit with $\eta^o$ and $\epsilon^o$. Faithfulness here is that of an equivalence on complete objects, not faithfulness of individual finite evaluations. All equations were equations of the specified system constructions before realization.
